correctness.rationale: For each surviving set, maximum matching size equals the finite recurrence optimum over all injective assignments. Independent pollinator survival gives an exact positive Bernstein-basis expectation. A complete search of \(2^{ab}\) binary incidence matrices for every ordered pair of positive guild sizes \(a+b\le8\) retains all connected cases and verifies componentwise comparison in every matched degree group: 70,492 labeled networks and 21 distinct coefficient-vector pairs. The two connected 4-by-5 witnesses share respective degree multisets; independently recomputed survivor coefficients are (0,5,19,27,17,4) and (0,5,20,26,14,3), yielding the exact polynomial (1-q)^2(1-2q^2) and unique interior crossing. The compiled checker and its independent witness assignment implementation ran to PASS.

value.rationale: Maximum bipartite matching counts simultaneously serviceable plant species when each available partner offers one unit of service. The sharp nine-species cutoff is a mathematically complete, naturally defined small-network boundary showing a degree-matched architecture with initially lower service capacity can overtake a higher-capacity architecture under severe independent partner losses. The exact crossing at \(1/\sqrt2\) is a replicable benchmark, not just an arbitrary parameter slice; scope is a constrained allocation model and no ecological efficacy claim is made.
